summary: Half-closed SSE session: early FIN from corporate TLS inspector leads to reconnect that drops closing list items and duplicates system preface
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinScale Labs) using Redwood Private in eu-west reported truncated Markdown lists and duplicated system lead-ins after an SSE stream disconnect and reconnect. Impact: final list items and the closing Markdown fence are missing in ~60% of reconnects; clients see a duplicated system message at the top of the resumed stream.

Impact:
- User-visible: incomplete bulleted lists in generated responses, often missing last 1-3 list items and trailing punctuation.
- Functional: downstream parsers (JSON/Markdown consumers) fail to validate conversation boundaries.
- Scope: multiple instances in customer's VPC across two dedicated nodes; observed in production only.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (customer-controlled edge in their VPC) behind corporate TLS inspection appliance (vendor: NetInspect X).
- Client: browser and server SDKs behind the customer's corp-proxy.
- Model: redwood-llama-13b pinned v2026-02-10.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a streaming completion (SSE) with a prompt that yields a bulleted list and a final paragraph.
2) After ~30–90s, trigger an outbound TLS re-inspect (customer's security appliance emits a FIN/close as it rotates session internals).
3) Client reconnects using the standard stream-resume flow.
4) Resumed stream contains: duplicated system preface line ("SYSTEM: Resuming..." injected by runtime for resumed sessions) and the final 1–3 bullet items from the original completion are missing.

Observed logs (edge + app):
- edge-proxy.log excerpt (during incident):
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.912Z] conn: socket=0x7f4fd FIN received from upstream (inspector)
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.915Z] conn: half-close: pipeline flushed, keepalive pending
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.916Z] sse: session-id=9802 resume-token=rtk_7f4fd queued-resume

- runtime.log excerpt:
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.918Z] stream: session=9802 state=HALF_CLOSED kvcache=warm
  [2026-03-10T14:12:08.120Z] stream: resume requested token=rtk_7f4fd last-offset=3472
  [2026-03-10T14:12:08.121Z] stream: emitted system-resume-envelope id=9802-preface
  [2026-03-10T14:12:08.122Z] stream: resume: rehydrate-kv start=3473 end=NNN

- client-side observation (customer): duplicated first "SYSTEM:" line and final bullet list items missing on DOM render.

Initial hypothesis:
- The TLS inspector's mid-stream FIN causes the edge-proxy to half-close the connection while the runtime believes the request is still in-flight. On resume, the runtime emits a system-resume envelope but does not reconcile the last in-flight token boundary properly; the reconstructor on the client sees the duplicated system preface and the final in-flight tokens are never re-sent (or are treated as already-delivered).
- Alternative: edge-proxy's flush during half-close clobbers the last fragment in the outgoing buffer and resume offset is computed using the flushed offset, not the truly delivered offset.

Logs/metrics links provided by customer:
- Edge dashboard: https://grafana.finscale.internal/d/streams/edge-latency
- Runtime trace: https://sentry.redwood.internal/trace/9802

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced in our lab when we simulated an upstream FIN from a TLS-inspector by sending a half-close during active SSE. Reproduction rate ~3/10.
- Observed that the runtime resume path re-emits a system-resume envelope unconditionally; client SDK prepends resumed fragments to the message buffer and treats the resume-envelope as a normal system message, resulting in apparent duplication.
- Verified that last-offset persisted by the edge component is sometimes one fragment lower than the runtime's internal last-seen-offset after a half-close. This mismatch correlates with missing trailing bullets.
- Correlated timing: if FIN occurs immediately after a chunk boundary, issue not observed; when FIN occurs mid-chunk (edge flush), final tokens are lost on resume.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Disable the TLS inspector's aggressive session rotation for flows to Redwood endpoints (they applied a policy to exempt the inference subnets). This reduced incidence to near-zero for their test traffic.
- Customer can increase client resume window: set resume_grace_period_ms to 5000 in client SDK to accept a wider offset delta while SDK merge logic is being upgraded.

Next steps and action items:
- Engineering (streaming/runtime) to add an idempotent marker to resume-envelope and ensure client SDK treats resume-envelope as a control-only marker (do not render). (PR referenced below).
- Edge team to align flushed-offset semantics with runtime last-seen-offset on half-close; add validation that resume offset <= runtime offset before marking resumed segments as delivered.
- Add telemetry to detect resume-offset mismatches and raise a metric/resume-offset-delta > 0.

Related artifacts:
- Repro harness used: tests/streaming/halfclose-repro (internal).
- Temporary client patch: sdk-js#v0.21.3-resume-control (customer applied locally).

Expected SLA commitments:
- Customer requested a live workaround confirmation within 24h (sla_due_at: 2026-03-11T16:00:00Z in their timezone).

investigation_notes: Simulated FIN reproduced missing trailing tokens; reproduction rate correlated with mid-chunk FINs.
Client SDK currently treats resume-envelope as a renderable system message; patch pending to treat as control-only.
Edge flush semantics differ between proxy implementations; added a test matrix for nginx, envoy, and the customer's NetInspect X appliance.
resolution_notes: Temporary: Customer exempted Redwood egress from TLS inspector rotations, reduced incidents to near-zero.
Short-term fix (runtime): emit resume-envelope with explicit control header resume-control:true so SDKs ignore in-rendering (PR runtime#1289).
Medium-term fix (edge): add guard to compute resume-offset based on runtime last-seen token; reject resume if offset mismatch > 4 tokens and trigger re-emit of missing fragments.
Follow-up: Add telemetry alert (resume-offset-delta) and include into Console per-route dashboard for Private deployments.
